title: Alibaba to ban employees from using Anthropic's coding tool, source says

reading.body:
This is a case of a deployed system carrying hidden logic that its users could not see. The markers were embedded in the system prompt of a coding agent and varied according to the user's API base URL and timezone, so the same tool behaved differently depending on where it was run. The mechanism was obfuscated, with domain and keyword lists stored as base64 strings decoded with an XOR key, which places the failure at the point of deployment rather than in any single model output.

The behaviour was conditional rather than universal. It stayed inactive for users on the official Anthropic endpoint or with no base URL set, and the reporting describes it as aimed at unauthorized gateways and model distillation. Catching it would have required inspecting the shipped prompt and binary rather than testing the tool's visible behaviour, since the markers were designed not to surface in normal use.

What is not established is intent. Anthropic has described the tracker as an experiment, and the reporting of a ban by Alibaba over alleged backdoor risks is an allegation and a corporate decision, not a finding of a backdoor.

reports.title: Claude Code Is Steganographically Marking Requests
Anthropic is removing its covert code for catching Chinese competitors
Claude Code’s hidden tracker was an “experiment,” says Anthropic
Alibaba to ban employees from using Anthropic's coding tool, source says

summary:
A blog post reported that Claude Code, Anthropic's coding agent, hides markers in its system prompt based on the user's API base URL and timezone. The code checks the ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL environment variable and the system timezone. If the timezone is Asia/Shanghai or Asia/Urumqi, the date separator changes from a hyphen to a slash. If the hostname matches a hidden list of domains or AI lab keywords, the apostrophe in the date sentence changes to different Unicode characters. The domain and keyword lists are stored as base64 strings decoded with an XOR key.

The lists include Chinese tech and AI companies plus many proxy and reseller domains. The author says the feature likely targets unauthorized gateways and model distillation, and that it stays inactive for users on the official Anthropic endpoint or with no base URL set. The article says the bypass is trivial, through changing the hostname, timezone, or patching the binary, and argues the behavior should have been documented openly.
